_comment: Capability contracts, so an orchestrator can compose labs it can introspect. This is NOT an inventory -- manifests/tools.json records what is installed. A capability here states what it consumes, the typed facts it produces, what it requires, what it proves, what it does NOT prove, and a negative control that must fail. 'state: observed' means the probe below was actually run; the summary is what it printed. Verify with: python scripts/registry-verify.py

fact_types.address: an address in the target's own address space, hex string, never reused across rebuilds
fact_types.string: a text literal recovered from the target
fact_types.structure: a typed record: named fields, each with an offset and a type
fact_types.bytes_ref: a pointer to content-addressed bytes under E:\missions\ or a lab out dir; the bytes are not inlined
fact_types.verdict: an outcome class from a closed enumeration: confirmed | likely | speculative | unresolved | refused
fact_types.path_ref: a filesystem path to an artifact; never the artifact's contents
fact_types.apk: a parsed Android package manifest or dex summary
fact_types.token: a parsed JOSE/JWT: header, claims, signature presence -- never a live credential

capabilities.title: Decompile native x86-64 code through IDA 9.2 headlessly

inputs.name: binary
inputs.note: Owner-named or self-built. Provenance must be checkable.

invalidates_on: the target is rebuilt -- every address in this output is void

reach.note: decompile itself only reads. The PROCESS it runs in does not: idalib-mcp can write a 2.7 MB .i64 to an arbitrary path via idb_save, which its own --unsafe tagging does NOT cover. So the trust boundary is the server, not the tool.

capabilities.gate_must_not_delegate_why: Measured on this host, not read: on a worker started WITHOUT --unsafe (py_eval absent from tools/list), one unauthenticated loopback form POST -- POST /config with apply_profile=1&profile_text=py_eval -- made py_eval callable and it returned 2. http.py:93 snapshots ORIGINAL_TOOLS at import time, BEFORE idalib_server.py:285-289 deletes the unsafe tools, and http.py:442-446 rebuilds tools.methods from that stale snapshot; _check_api_request (mcp.py:303-328) accepts any request carrying no Origin header, so no token is needed. The result is persisted into the IDB netnode $ ida_mcp.enabled_tools (http.py:447), so the policy travels inside the sample's .i64. Two further holes: idb_open/idb_list are `protected` from --profile (idalib_server.py:57-60), and the supervisor never applies --profile to its own registry (idalib_supervisor.py:1498-1499 only forwards it to workers), so a 'read-only' profile still grants arbitrary-path file access. Our gate enforces this; the server's own flags do not.

envelope.success_when: body.code is non-null AND body.error is absent

session.why: Observed live: a supervisor's idb_open ADOPTED another process's idalib worker through the shared discovery files, then lost the session on the very next call. A session id is not a durable handle.

proves: that a named function's machine code decompiles to the C shown, on those exact bytes
which strings and imports the recovered logic references
does_not_prove: that the decompilation is faithful -- it is one analyser's reconstruction
anything about a binary whose provenance was not established
anything dynamic: no runtime value, no breakpoint, no memory state
side_effects: spawns an idalib worker bound to 127.0.0.1:8745

negative_control.command: decompile addr=0xDEADBEEF on the open session
negative_control.why: must yield code:null plus an error field, never code. Asserted by native-lab/tools/loop.mjs.

capabilities.title: Enumerate functions in a native binary

inputs.name: queries
inputs.note: one round trip carries N queries; that batching is the reason to use this server at all

envelope.success_when: every requested query has a result object AND result.length == queries.length

batch.aggregate: require len(result) == len(queries); a short result is a FAILURE, not a smaller answer

envelope.why: Measured, not read: normalize_dict_list silently DROPS non-dict elements in a mixed list (utils.py:704-706) -- 5 queries in, 4 results out, with no index, no echo and no dropped counter. An empty array becomes [{}] and returns one bogus failed item (utils.py:694-695). Past the 50,000-char response cap (rpc.py:20) the WHOLE result is replaced by a 10-item preview plus output_truncated and a download URL: measured 6,000 get_int requests came back as 10 items and 417,213 characters truncated. An orchestrator that asked for five facts and read four answers would otherwise have no signal that anything went missing.

session.why: a session id was observed adopted across processes via shared discovery files, then lost on the next call

proves: which functions the analyser recovered, with their addresses and sizes
does_not_prove: that the function list is complete -- inlined and unreachable code is routinely missed
that a recovered boundary matches the author's intent

negative_control.why: must refuse rather than answer from an unstated session

capabilities.title: Drive and observe a page over the Chrome DevTools Protocol

inputs.name: url
inputs.note: loopback origins only unless a gate verdict exists

proves: what a loopback page rendered and returned at the time it was asked
does_not_prove: anything about a host we have no verdict for
that behaviour is stable -- the page was observed once, at one moment

negative_control.why: the CA must not be trusted outside the lab instance; ISOLATION HELD is the passing state and a broken pin must not

capabilities.title: Parse and verify JOSE/JWT structure without accepting it as valid
proves: the token's structure, claims and declared algorithm
does_not_prove: that a token is valid, unexpired, or unforgeable
that a claimed algorithm matches the one the server enforces
anything about a live credential -- nothing here consumes or stores one

negative_control.command: oracle with an alg=none and a swapped-claims token
negative_control.why: a structurally valid token that must not be accepted as verified

capabilities.title: Parse captures and infer protocol format and state machine
proves: what the recorded flows contained, and how the analyser classified them
does_not_prove: that a session was legitimate -- capture records traffic, not authority
anything about traffic we did not capture

probe.last_summary: 16 questions, request/response rewriting and isolation checks passed

negative_control.why: isolation must fail loudly if the lab CA is trusted outside its instance

capabilities.title: Parse memory and host artefacts, and treat refusals as results
proves: which artefacts the parsers recovered from the image
that Volatility 3 refused the synthetic image, which is the point of the check
does_not_prove: that absence of an artefact means absence of the behaviour
any conclusion resting on a single tool family -- corroboration needs a second capability

probe.last_summary: 37 checks (74 PASS lines -- each check prints a verdict and its evidence)

negative_control.command: drop SRUM from the image and re-run
negative_control.why: the conclusion must degrade from confirmed to possible, proving the triangulation rule is live

capabilities.title: Decompile managed .NET assemblies and detect wrong-answer paths
proves: that each sample's answer was recovered from its own decompilation and confirmed against its output
does_not_prove: that a recovery generalises beyond the sample it was recovered from
that a confident answer is a correct one -- see the wrong-entry-state control

probe.last_summary: 27 checks (46 PASS lines -- count unique names, not rows)

negative_control.command: m02's solver pointed at m01's assembly
negative_control.why: it produces a complete, confident, WRONG answer; the harness must reject it. This is the station's canonical failure mode.

capabilities.title: Build and statically analyse a real signed APK

invalidates_on: the APK is rebuilt or re-signed

proves: what the APK's manifest, DEX and native library contain as built
does_not_prove: anything about runtime behaviour -- no device, so ART acceptance, on-device TLS and .so execution are NOT claimed
packing or anti-emulator detection, which this lab does not implement yet
Kotlin name recovery, which R8's retained metadata makes possible and we do not yet do

negative_control.command: cross-check AXML with a second independent decoder
negative_control.why: one decoder agreeing with itself is not corroboration; pyelftools already caught a real sh_link bug this way

capabilities.title: Solve self-built crackmes and record the technique used
proves: that each crackme was solved, and by which named technique
does_not_prove: that the technique transfers to a binary we did not build

negative_control.command: c01's solver pointed at c02's binary
negative_control.why: a technique label must not be emitted for a sample it did not solve

capabilities.title: Instrument a live Android device with Frida

reach.note: admin=true is declared as fs_write and proc_spawn rather than left implicit, because a decorator tag can miss an effect. Frida injects into a running process and writes to the device, so the effect is real even while the capability is absent.

does_not_prove: that any on-device behaviour was observed -- there is no device on this host
ART accepting our scripts, live on-device TLS interception, or .so disassembly

probe.last_summary: adb is not on PATH; no device and no emulator is installed

negative_control.command: any Frida attach while adb reports no device
negative_control.why: must refuse rather than silently degrading to the logic-only suite and claiming the same coverage

capabilities.title: Mutation-fuzz this repository's own parsers under a differential oracle

inputs.name: target
inputs.note: one of pcap | jose | forensic-pf | web-triage. All four parsers are ours.

artifacts.note: gitignored on purpose -- a reproducer is hostile input against the parsers we ship. The recipe is committed; replay re-derives the bytes and checks the hash.

invalidates_on: a parser is fixed -- the finding moves to the regression guard

proves: that four specific parsers in this tree survived or did not survive a mutation campaign, with the outcome of every input recorded
that the harness can distinguish a parser that DECLARES its refusals from one that crashes -- rejected is handled, uncaught is a finding
that each recorded finding reproduces from its recipe alone, after minimisation
does_not_prove: that a `rejected` outcome is CORRECT -- the lab proves the parser returned a decision, not the right one, and a parser rejecting everything would pass every reference assertion
anything about a parser outside the four-target set, or about coverage beyond the 27-seed corpus
anything about tshark, Wireshark, jadx, Volatility or DiE -- installed third-party parsers are deliberately NOT targets, because a finding there is not a finding about this tree
native memory safety -- there is no ASAN or UBSAN, and the 192 MB ceiling is a V8 heap cap, so a 1-byte out-of-bounds read inside a Buffer is invisible to it
side_effects: spawns roughly two child processes per input; about 11 min at the default budget of 60

probe.last_summary: 24/24 assertions, 480 inputs, 1 live reference finding, 12 flawed-twin findings, 6/6 regressions holding

negative_control.command: run the campaign against each target's deliberately flawed twin
negative_control.why: a run in which any flawed twin SURVIVES fails. Each twin has exactly one guard removed, in the way an analyst actually makes the mistake. The pcap twin's defect is silent -- Buffer.subarray clamps, so it reports capturedLength 1000 while returning 4 bytes, which a crash-counting fuzzer cannot see. That is the whole argument for a differential oracle over a crash counter.

provenance.source: measured on this host 2026-09-30; four real defects found and fixed in this tree
